justification: The requirement and progress are stated directly, and the claim control is disabled until the completed-ad threshold is reached; the interface is not hiding the condition.
vision_observation: The sheet shows Exporter Pro cards at 0/10 through 3/10 with visible reward bars, a Watch ad action, and a visually present Claim HD export control.
dom_observation: Every rendered state exposes 0 to 3 completed ads and marks Claim HD export disabled with cursor-not-allowed while the Watch ad action adds one completed ad.
semantic_observation: The text consistently says ten rewarded ads are required and labels the progress as completed ads, with the claim action shown alongside each early progress state.

justification: The signup view omits renewal and cancellation information while the cancellation view uses extreme irreversible-loss warnings and a confirmshaming label, creating a clear asymmetric flow.
vision_observation: The rendered signup card says free trial with Start free trial, while the cancellation card lists catastrophic consequences and uses I still want to cancel.
dom_observation: The DOM explicitly notes no renewal or cancellation mention on signup and presents an alarming irreversible cancellation paragraph with a reluctant confirmation button.
semantic_observation: The semantic states contrast a friendly trial offer lacking billing terms with a cancellation screen that threatens loss of benefits, data, access, and remaining time.

justification: A single required-looking checkbox bundles Terms, Privacy, and third-party data sharing, so accepting the service appears to require consent to an optional data practice.
vision_observation: The sheet shows one unchecked checkbox covering three agreements, including third-party data sharing, beside a prominent Create account button.
dom_observation: The DOM has one checkbox whose label combines Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, and third-party data-sharing agreements; the account button is disabled before ticking it.
semantic_observation: The text says acceptance occurs only when the box is actively ticked, but it still presents the optional partner data-sharing consent as part of that same bundled agreement.

justification: The progression shows explicit forge counts, levels, and gold totals; increasing requirements are visible rather than concealed and no contradictory charge or outcome is shown.
vision_observation: The visual sheet presents Level 1 through Level 3 cards with plainly displayed 0/1, 0/2, 1/2, and 0/3 forge progress and two labeled forge actions.
dom_observation: The DOM exposes each level requirement, progressbar value, gold earned so far, and the same +1 and Forge x5 controls in every state.
semantic_observation: The semantic states describe a fair curve with visible requirements increasing from one to three forges and predictable ten-gold rewards.

justification: The purchase uses vague exclusive framing and a saved payment method for a fee while failing to state what the chest actually provides; the small price disclosure does not cure the opaque benefit.
vision_observation: The sheet shows a Mysterious Ancient Chest, a prominent unlock button, faint 4.99 dollar text, and a later Chest unlocked state without any concrete contents or benefit.
dom_observation: The DOM calls the fee small and charges 4.99 to the payment method on file, while the only benefit wording is enhance your journey and the post-action state gives no item detail.
semantic_observation: The semantic text describes a legendary sealed chest and then merely reports that it was unlocked, leaving the paid outcome undefined and relying on the payment method on file.

justification: The subscription choices are presented with equal access, the current and renewal prices are explicit, and cancellation is stated to take effect at period end.
vision_observation: The sheet shows four same-sized options—keep, pause, downgrade, and cancel—in an even grid, with renewal date and both rates visible.
dom_observation: All four buttons have equivalent styling and the DOM states aria-pressed selection explicitly; the copy says cancellation is effective at the end of the current period.
semantic_observation: The text discloses Aug 17, the 59-dollar current rate, the 99-dollar standard renewal rate, and equal reachability for all choices.

justification: The displayed 98 percent five-star statistic cannot correspond exactly to a whole-number count of twelve reviews, making the social-proof claim materially misleading.
vision_observation: The product cards prominently show 98% of 12 customer reviews rate the product 5 stars, repeated beside Buy now actions.
dom_observation: The DOM renders the exact claim 98% of 12 customer reviews rate this product 5 stars with no qualification or rounding explanation.
semantic_observation: The semantic channel repeats the 98-percent and twelve-review figures, which visibly do not form a plausible exact review fraction.

justification: The five-second pre-roll requirement is repeatedly disclosed and the ad-length promise is consistent; the state variation identifies the ad rather than concealing it.
vision_observation: The sheet labels each episode pre-roll: 5s ad and shows an Ad sponsor block with a 5s duration, alongside Play or ad 5s controls.
dom_observation: The DOM header says one 5-second ad before each episode and every episode row carries pre-roll: 5s ad; the playback state exposes the ad duration.
semantic_observation: The semantic states consistently state that the free plan has one five-second ad per episode and that ad length never changes.

justification: The checkout promotes an unexplained Recommended option and SAVE 20% claim without showing a comparison basis, while the purchase flow can still appear active after an order is placed.
vision_observation: The rendered sheet emphasizes a Recommended option badge and SAVE 20% around Complete purchase, yet shows no reference plan or original price and also shows an Order placed panel.
dom_observation: The DOM gives the annual Pro Plan a Recommended option badge and a SAVE 20% overlay while exposing only the 89-dollar price, tax, and total due today.
semantic_observation: The semantic state lists the annual plan, tax, total, recommendation, and savings badge but supplies no baseline for the savings or explanation of the post-purchase presentation.

justification: The permission request names the camera and microphone needed for a video call, offers Not now, and explicitly marks location as optional; no unrelated permission is required.
vision_observation: The sheet alternates a Join video call card with a clearly worded camera-and-microphone request that includes a Not now option and says location is optional.
dom_observation: The DOM permission panel explicitly requests camera and microphone, provides Not now, and states that location can be shared only if wanted.
semantic_observation: The semantic states preserve the same call context, permission purpose, optional-location wording, and two available choices.

justification: The quest promises energy for a six-second ad but the ad state says it is skippable after one second, creating a direct mismatch in the required viewing condition.
vision_observation: The visual shows Watch ad to earn 1 Energy (6s) above an ad with a 0:06 timer, Skip ad control, and Skippable after 1s text.
dom_observation: The DOM combines the six-second energy button with a sponsored ad state whose controls include disabled Skip ad initially and copy saying skippable after 1s while the ad still plays.
semantic_observation: The semantic text repeats the six-second reward requirement and the one-second skip disclosure, so the user-facing conditions conflict.

justification: The promotion uses unsupported urgency and an ambiguous savings number: SAVE 50 does not identify percent, currency, product scope, or the actual discounted price.
vision_observation: The sheet prominently shows TechNook flash sale, Ends tonight, and SAVE 50 above a large Claim offer button with only tiny terms text.
dom_observation: The DOM contains Ends tonight, SAVE 50, Limited time offer. Terms apply., and no original price, currency, percentage, or qualifying product detail.
semantic_observation: The semantic state repeats the same ambiguous savings claim and deadline language without adding a concrete offer basis or duration.

justification: The ticket price is foregrounded while processing and service charges are relegated to tiny secondary text and no prominently combined payable total is shown.
vision_observation: The visual emphasizes 49 dollars per ticket and a large Book ticket button, while the fee line is very small beneath a divider.
dom_observation: The DOM presents 49.00 per ticket and separately places processing fee 6.50 and service charge 3.25 in an eight-pixel button-like line.
semantic_observation: The semantic channel lists the base ticket price and additional charges but never presents the combined amount as the primary booking price.

justification: The optional donation uses direct guilt and personification to pressure payment, and the completed state still leaves prominent support prompts visible.
vision_observation: The sheet shows Coco looking right at you and would be so happy if helped beside a large Support now button, followed by Support recorded.
dom_observation: The DOM calls the 2.99 contribution entirely optional but places it next to text saying Coco is watching and would be happy if the user paid.
semantic_observation: The semantic states pair the optional one-time amount with emotional solicitation and then report the contribution recorded without removing the repeated solicitation context.

justification: The interface intentionally shows one current price equal to the legally relevant 30-day low and explicitly avoids a false comparison anchor.
vision_observation: The sheet shows PLN 199.00 as both the current and 30-day lowest price, with a Single price badge and no crossed-out former price.
dom_observation: The DOM contains one price node, a matching 30-day baseline, and an explanation that no secondary price or anchor exists.
semantic_observation: The semantic states explicitly say no other price is shown and that the baseline is stated factually under the EU Omnibus Directive.

justification: The product uses live-viewer social proof that changes across states and is explicitly labeled Fabricated metric, making the scarcity signal artificial.
vision_observation: The sheet shows 37, 64, and 50 people watching/viewing the same headphones and labels later panels Fabricated metric.
dom_observation: The DOM changes the watching count across states, keeps the product action in an added state, and adds a Fabricated metric callout.
semantic_observation: The semantic text records the watcher counts and directly names the displayed metric fabricated, confirming misleading social proof.

justification: Autoplay is already enabled and the next episode is starting in seconds; although a switch exists, the screen foregrounds automatic continuation without an explicit neutral choice before playback.
vision_observation: The sheet shows Autoplay: ON, Episode 4, and a countdown to automatic start with the toggle visibly on.
dom_observation: The DOM exposes aria-checked true and states the next episode will play automatically, with no separate cancel or defer control.
semantic_observation: The semantic state consistently describes autoplay enabled and starting in three seconds, indicating a pre-enabled continuation setting.

justification: Video playback starts automatically merely because the media is in view, without a visible user play action or stop control, making the behavior intrusive and non-consensual.
vision_observation: The visual shows a Playing badge, auto label, active progress, and text saying playback started automatically because the video is in view.
dom_observation: The DOM marks the media Playing with 11 percent progress and explicitly states playback started automatically because the video is in view.
semantic_observation: The semantic state repeats auto playback and the in-view trigger, with no user-initiated play step represented.

justification: The discount and countdown are explicitly tied to a server-validated reservation deadline, and the payment state transition is clearly labeled rather than hidden.
vision_observation: The sheet shows 89 dollars versus 129 dollars, a reservation countdown marked server-validated, and a later Paid check state.
dom_observation: The DOM states that the price reverts when the server-validated deadline passes and changes Pay 89.00 to Paid checkmark after payment.
semantic_observation: The semantic states provide the same product, price reversion condition, server-validated expiry, and explicit paid outcome.

justification: The virtual-currency purchase places an approximate real-money equivalent next to the gem amount and clearly labels the item cosmetic-only; the later panel explicitly describes full-size disclosure.
vision_observation: The sheet shows 4,500 Gems together with approximately 45 dollars, a cosmetic-only description, and a Full-size real-price disclosure panel.
dom_observation: The DOM renders the real-money equivalent beside the gem price, says no stat changes, and includes the full-size disclosure state.
semantic_observation: The semantic text says users would know the approximate 45-dollar cost before clicking and that no secondary price is hidden.

justification: The English cookie banner presents the rejection action and privacy-settings link only in French despite explicitly identifying the site language and locale as English en-US.
vision_observation: The sheet shows Accept all cookies in English but Refuser les cookies non essentiels and the privacy link in French, with English locale metadata.
dom_observation: The rejection button has lang=fr while the surrounding copy says Site language: English and Your locale: en-US.
semantic_observation: The semantic states repeat the mixed-language controls and then report preferences saved without showing which choice was stored.

justification: Installing the advertised 18.4 GB base game silently writes optional premium content regardless, with no checkbox or opt-out while storage impact is presented as the base install.
vision_observation: The installer calls itself an 18.4 GB base game but its EULA says optional premium payload is written regardless; the other state shows Writing files.
dom_observation: The DOM explicitly says there is no checkbox and the payload is written regardless, while the install button names only the 18.4 GB base game.
semantic_observation: The semantic states preserve the no-checkbox EULA, optional premium content placement, and transition to writing files.

justification: The flow treats an ordinary login as consent to cancel account deletion and restore the account, with no separate confirmation of that intent.
vision_observation: The sheet says Log in to cancel, offers Log in now or Wait 30 days, and later reports deletion cancelled after a habitual login.
dom_observation: The DOM states that signing back in is assumed to mean changed intent and that the deletion request is cancelled and account restored.
semantic_observation: The semantic text explicitly explains that muscle memory login was interpreted as a keep-account request rather than routine access.

justification: The trial choice is visually dominant, declining is framed as merely keeping ads, and the shown offer omits renewal price, billing date, and cancellation terms.
vision_observation: The sheet gives a large Yes, start my free trial now button and a small No, I will just keep reading ads alternative, followed by Trial started.
dom_observation: The DOM uses the same imbalanced labels and reports a seven-day trial without stating the post-trial charge or renewal conditions.
semantic_observation: The semantic states contain the paywall, trial-start outcome, and ad-framed decline but no billing or cancellation disclosure.

justification: A flashlight advertised as entirely local requests permission to upload contacts to servers even though the user can use the flashlight without that access.
vision_observation: The sheet places a local flashlight card beside a contacts-upload permission panel with Allow access and Not now.
dom_observation: The DOM says the utility works entirely on the device, then asks to upload the address book and admits the flashlight remains usable without it.
semantic_observation: The semantic states repeat the contradiction between local operation and server upload, with the permission prompt recurring in both on and off states.

justification: The insurance selector uses vague coverage descriptions and an unsupported Most popular badge to steer choice, while omitting concrete coverage differences needed for comparison.
vision_observation: The sheet shows eight similarly structured policy cards with sparse descriptions and Premium Plus marked Most popular, plus only a generic Choose a policy button.
dom_observation: The DOM exposes eight radio options with prices and generic added-benefits wording; Premium Plus alone carries the Most popular marker and no coverage details are shown.
semantic_observation: The semantic channel lists the eight prices and repetitive descriptions but provides no limits, exclusions, or basis for the popularity claim.

justification: The reward is fixed and repeatedly disclosed as four coins per play, so the game-like presentation does not conceal a random or variable outcome.
vision_observation: The visual sheet shows balances increasing by four and banners saying same as last time and predictable rewards.
dom_observation: The DOM records 0, 4, 8, and 12 coins with four coins each and a matching +4 result after plays.
semantic_observation: The semantic states explicitly call the rewards predictable and show the same fixed increment at each play count.

justification: The order auto-confirms in 13 seconds even though the displayed terms take about 60 seconds to read, creating forced urgency and automatic purchase without a visible opt-out.
vision_observation: The sheet shows a 00:13 countdown to auto-confirm beside terms labeled approximately 60s reading time and a Confirm purchase now button.
dom_observation: The DOM states that the order auto-confirms at 00:00, shows 00:13, and lists recurring 49-dollar monthly renewal and no-refund terms.
semantic_observation: The semantic state repeats the short timer, longer reading estimate, automatic renewal, and no-refund condition before the confirmed state.

justification: An optional 19.99 extended warranty is included in the initial cart total and must be explicitly declined to return to the 129.99 base price.
vision_observation: The sheet shows optional protection inside the cart with an initial Pay 149.98 total, then a Declined state at 129.99.
dom_observation: The DOM includes the warranty in the first total and provides Decline—remove from order; later states say it is excluded and total 129.99.
semantic_observation: The semantic states explicitly distinguish the initial 149.98 amount from the warranty-declined 129.99 amount, confirming default inclusion of the add-on.

justification: The promotional dialog explicitly makes its close control evade the cursor and hints at an unexplained consequence, obstructing ordinary dismissal.
vision_observation: The sheet shows a Special offer panel with an X close control and text saying the X runs away from the cursor.
dom_observation: The DOM exposes a close dialog button but its adjacent copy says the X runs away and something else happens if caught.
semantic_observation: The semantic state repeats the 20-percent offer and the stated evasive-close behavior without explaining the consequence.

justification: The inventory quantity is stated consistently and accompanied by an explicit honest-inventory explanation that it matches the backend quantity, without manufactured scarcity.
vision_observation: The sheet shows the same 148 available badge on both cart states and an Honest inventory callout.
dom_observation: The DOM consistently renders In stock—148 available and transitions only the cart button from Add to cart to Added to cart.
semantic_observation: The semantic state says displayed quantity equals true quantity and explicitly says there is no manufactured scarcity or FOMO trigger.

justification: The feed identifies the number of reels, provides an explicit Load more action, and states that continuation requires affirmative action; semantic states show additional distinct entries rather than fabricated progress.
vision_observation: The visible viewport repeats the first few rows while counters rise from 6 to 18 and a Load more reels control remains present, consistent with a scrollable feed.
dom_observation: The DOM uses an overflow-y-auto Reel feed region and explicit Load more reels control; state content contains the corresponding larger item sets.
semantic_observation: The semantic states enumerate distinct 6-, 10-, 14-, and 18-reel feeds and say continuation requires explicit affirmative action.

justification: The destructive Delete account action is styled and positioned exactly like benign Save changes, with no warning or confirmation safeguard and only an eight-pixel gap.
vision_observation: The sheet shows equal purple Save changes and Delete account buttons side by side in both settings states.
dom_observation: The DOM gives both actions identical full-width flex styling and explicitly notes the delete action is inside the safety-margin radius.
semantic_observation: The semantic text calls out identical weight, side-by-side placement, and the saved state without any deletion confirmation.

justification: The plan headline and feature bullets promise unlimited storage and projects, but fine print directly imposes a 5 GB cap and three-project limit.
vision_observation: The sheet prominently says CloudPlus Pro—Unlimited and lists unlimited storage and unlimited projects above a smaller Fine print box with restrictive caps.
dom_observation: The DOM places Unlimited feature rows before a lower-contrast fine-print statement that storage is capped at 5 GB and projects limited to 3.
semantic_observation: The semantic state repeats the contradictory unlimited claims and the exact restrictive limits next to the 12-dollar monthly choice.

justification: Each setting control exposes current state and next action in the label, and the explanatory text matches the resulting sharing state; there is no hidden outcome.
vision_observation: The sheet shows Data sharing controls labeled Off—turn on or On—turn off, with matching descriptions and Feedforward present callouts.
dom_observation: The DOM pairs the off description with Off—turn on and the shared-with-12-partners description with On—turn off across all states.
semantic_observation: The semantic states explicitly say the switch wording and eventual sharing outcome match, while unrelated 2FA and notification states remain consistent.

justification: The interface reports an active 29-dollar monthly subscription and charge while still presenting an unfinished Step 2 signup, and marketing emails are enabled without a visible choice.
vision_observation: The sheet shows Step 2 of 3 with Next and Back while a separate panel already says Subscription active and Charged 29.00.
dom_observation: The DOM exposes the plan and auto-renewal terms, then an active subscription state reporting a charge and marketing emails enabled before the shown flow is complete.
semantic_observation: The semantic states place the charged active subscription alongside the still-in-progress plan step and note marketing emails enabled with no consent control.

justification: Required service consent and six optional partner agreements are separated, all optional boxes start empty, and each partner requires an explicit tick.
vision_observation: The sheet clearly separates the required ChatLoop agreement from six unchecked optional partner rows, each with a view terms link.
dom_observation: The DOM has one required ChatLoop checkbox, six independent partner checkboxes, a 0 of 6 selected count, and text saying partners bind only when explicitly ticked.
semantic_observation: The semantic state says users may accept desired agreements and decline the rest, with no partner agreement preselected.
